lesson.text: Quick memory: what number do you call in an emergency? ({number}.) Today: what to do when someone suddenly feels poorly.
Someone is poorly or hurt: tell a grown-up. Every bump on the head: tell a grown-up, even a small one.
A nosebleed: sit down, lean forward, and tell a grown-up. Never tip the head back.
Too hot in the sun and dizzy: help them into the shade, with sips of water, and tell a grown-up.
Lips swelling after eating? That can be an allergy: tell a grown-up straight away. No grown-up near: call {number} and say what happened and where.
Try it in the world: open the practice playground. Next: nosebleeds, asthma and the heat, on the Middle track.

Swelling lips after eating can be an allergy.
Calling for help: put it in order.
